newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Ex-warlord Taylor sworn in as Liberia's president.
newsitem.headline: Ex-warlord Taylor sworn in as Liberia's president.

text.p: Former warlord Charles Taylor was sworn in as Liberia's president on Saturday, marking the completion of a transition from seven years of civil war.
About a dozen heads of state or their representatives attended the colourful ceremony in the centre of the war-battered capital Monrovia.

"The event here today is the culmination of the collective efforts of the sub-region to restore peace to Liberia," Nigerian military ruler Genral Sani Abacha said in a speech on behalf of regional leaders who brokered peace in Liberia. Abacha heads the West African bloc, ECOWAS.
Taylor took the oath of office from Chief Justice Francis Johnson-Morris as African peacekeepers fired a 21-gun salute.

In 1989 Taylor launched the civil war that devastated the country founded by freed American slaves in 1847. But Liberians looking for strong leadership after the war voted massively for him in presidential elections on July 19.
